conclusions: Whole-inode returned/decoded metadata grows from8860 to66678 bytes per4KiB ACK while SQL notifications remain17/ACK; two complete decodes and one serialization remain a CPU/read amplification seam.

Native VFS confirmed write bytes remain about7.8-8.0 times payload and sync calls about2.02/ACK; immutable blob and inode publication remain two durable commits. These ratios do not establish physical SSD write amplification.
SDK successful blob input is exactly1x payload and old blob reads are0 for aligned hot overwrites; these arms provide no evidence that chunk compression fixes the metadata/commit seams.

CPU/ACK is stable within each extent pair and higher for larger files; throughput has material order/durability variation, including a21percent difference between32extent repeats, so neither a pure metadata causal percentage nor a production capacity limit is established.

Bounded lazy Drive runtime activation is a separate scale seam: current test workers and CLI startup eagerly open all catalog Drives. Static sharding would violate existing any-server route qualification.
limitations: One local macOS process with ten coordinator replicas; test wire helpers and synthetic auth bypass production remote provider and native mount. Not10 real servers,10k clients or10M files.
Only aligned writes, depth1 and one file per Drive; no read/mixed/unaligned/churn or compressed-content comparison.

Larger file population changes initial SQLite/B-tree/pager state and retained runtime state; faster arms accumulate more immutable blob history during fixed-duration runs. Warmup/checkpoint state and host drift remain confounders.

Two short balanced repeats per extent size are diagnostic observations, not steady-state statistical qualification. Audit/observer costs remain; inclusive/parallel wall timings overlap and cannot be summed as exclusive CPU.

SQLite metadata and blobs share physical files; VFS roles cannot attribute all work exclusively to one logical API. End totals are after reset, not end-minus-begin. Process accounting is distinct from VFS; host device remains unselected.
No allocation measurement, whole-client zero-allocation, crash/power-loss, Linux/macOS native mounts, hosted CI or full production-capacity claim.
Full-target dimensions and64GiB free-disk floor remain unchanged;24GiB RSS limit is per process, not fleet total.
